title: PiecePlan
description: A piece: a key, a tempo and parts in order.

bpm.description: Tempo in beats per minute, 40 to 200.

feel.description: How eighth notes are played. Use the groove "shuffle" or "triplets" with a shuffle feel.

key.description:
Key of the piece: a note name, "m" after it for minor. Examples: "G", "F#m", "Bb".
The piece ends on this key's tonic chord.

parts.description:
The parts in playing order, 1 to 16 parts and at most 160 bars in all (every part
counted `times` times).

title.description: Name of the piece, 1 to 80 characters. Progress is kept per title.

Drums.description: How much the drums play under a part.

oneOf.description: Kick, snare and hi-hat; a snare fill on the last beat before the next part.
Kick and hi-hat only (an intro); still gets the snare fill into the next part.

PieceFeel.description: How the eighth notes are played.

oneOf.description: Swung eighths (2:1); the metronome clicks the triplet.

PlanLine.description: What the bass plays; the groove gives the rhythm.

oneOf.description: The groove on the chord's root (the groove's own octaves and fifths stay).
As roots, a fifth on the third beat of the bar.

The root on beat one, then the third, fifth and seventh (or octave) of the chord on
the following beats.
A walking line in quarter notes (the groove's rhythm is ignored, the drums follow it).

As roots; the last note before a chord change leads to the next root by a half or
whole step.

PlanPart.description: One part of the form, e.g. a verse, played `times` in a row.

bars.description:
One entry per bar (1 to 16 bars), the chord symbols of that bar separated by a space.
One chord fills the bar, two chords split it in halves: "C G". Symbols are a note name
("C", "F#", "Bb") plus an optional quality: "" (major), m, 5, 6, m6, 7, maj7, m7, m7b5
(or ø), dim, dim7, sus2, sus4, 7sus4, add9, aug; "/" and a note names the bass note:
"C/E". Example: ["G", "D", "Em", "C"]; with a split bar ["Am", "Dm G", "C", "C"].

fill.description: The last beat of the part becomes a short run to the first note of the next part.

groove.description:
Rhythm of the bass, one of: quarters, eighths, sixteenths, rests, shuffle, octaves,
ghost, rootfifth, rootfifthoctave, dead, offbeat, tresillo, triplets, funk, slap,
staccato (all in 4/4; "rests" leaves the beat out, "rootfifth" is two half notes).

line.description: What the bass plays over the groove.

section.description: What the part is; it names the rehearsal mark over its first bar.

times.description: How often the bars are played in a row, 1 to 8.

Section.description: Where a part stands in the form.
